paper.title: Bayesian Optimization for Categorical and Category-Specific Continuous Inputs

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit-BO, sequential setting (categorical + category-specific continuous inputs)
unmapped: Action space is a union over K categories of category-specific continuous domains X_c in R^d, with an independent GP prior f_c ~ GP(0, k_c) per category
Maximum information gain of each kernel grows as gamma_T ~ O(T^alpha) with 0 <= alpha < 1 (Assumption 2)
GP sample paths have partial derivatives with sub-Gaussian tails (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: given an input $[c,x_{c}]$ and a black-box function $f([c,x_{c}])$, where $c\in\{1,...,C\}$ is a category among $C$ categories and $x_{c}\in\mathcal{X}_{c}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ are continuous variables corresponding to the category $c$, our goal is to find: [c^*,x^*]=argmax f([c,x_c])

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit-BO, batch setting (categorical + category-specific continuous inputs)
unmapped: Batches of fixed size B (feedback observed only after each batch of B evaluations); T = number of rounds x B
Action space is a union over K categories of category-specific continuous domains X_c in R^d, with an independent GP prior per category
Maximum information gain gamma_T ~ O(T^alpha), 0 <= alpha < 1 (Assumption 2)
GP sample paths have partial derivatives with sub-Gaussian tails (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: We extend our sequential method to batch setting to recommend a set of $B$ samples at each round. We note that the number of total function evaluations $T$ = the number of rounds $N$ $\times$ the batch size $B$.

conditions: f_c ~ GP(0,k_c) independently for each category
Assumption 1: GP sample-path partial derivatives satisfy P(|df/dx_i|<L) >= 1 - d r exp(-L^2/s^2)
Assumption 2: maximum information gain gamma_T ~ O(T^alpha) with 0 <= alpha < 1

source.label: lem:MAB_regret_Seq
source.quote: Let $f_{c}(x)\sim\text{GP}_{c}(0,k_{c}),c=1,...,C$ and $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ be the noisy function observation set suggested by our method in the sequential setting under the observation model $y_{i}=f_{c_{i}}(x_{i})+\epsilon_{i}$, where $\epsilon_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{\epsilon}^{2})$, then under Assumptions 1 and 2, we have $R_{T}^{\text{MAB}}\leq\mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{CT^{\alpha+1}\log T}\right)$.

results.notes: Bounds the 'MAB' component of the Bayesian regret: E sum_t [f_{c*}(x*) - f_{c_t}(x*_{c_t})]. Paper's C (number of categories) mapped to K. Quantity 'other' since it is one component of Bayesian regret.

conditions: f_c ~ GP(0,k_c) independently for each category
Assumption 1: GP sample-path partial derivatives satisfy P(|df/dx_i|<L) >= 1 - d r exp(-L^2/s^2)
Assumption 2: maximum information gain gamma_T ~ O(T^alpha) with 0 <= alpha < 1

source.label: lem:BO_regret_seq
source.quote: Let $f_{c}(x)\sim\text{GP}_{c}(0,k_{c}),c=1,...,C$ and $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ be the noisy function observation set suggested by our method in the sequential setting under the observation model $y_{i}=f_{c_{i}}(x_{i})+\epsilon_{i}$, where $\epsilon_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{\epsilon}^{2})$, then under Assumptions 1 and 2, we have $R_{T}^{\text{BO}}\leq\mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{CT^{\alpha+1}\log T}\right)$.

results.notes: Bounds the 'BO' component of the Bayesian regret: E sum_t [f_{c_t}(x*_{c_t}) - f_{c_t}(x_t)]. Quantity 'other' since it is one component of Bayesian regret.

conditions: f_c ~ GP(0,k_c) independently for each category
Assumption 1: GP sample-path partial derivatives satisfy P(|df/dx_i|<L) >= 1 - d r exp(-L^2/s^2)
Assumption 2: maximum information gain gamma_T ~ O(T^alpha) with 0 <= alpha < 1

source.label: thm:Overall-Bayesian-regret-Seq
source.quote: Under Assumptions 1 and 2, the Bayesian regret for our method after $T$ iterations in the sequential setting is bounded as $\text{BayesRegret}\left(T\right)\leq\mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{CT^{\alpha+1}\text{log}T}\right)$

results.notes: Paper's C = number of categories (arms), mapped to K. alpha is the information-gain growth exponent, not strong convexity, hence renamed. Proof is a sketch built on Russo & Van Roy.

symbols.psi_B: Desautels et al. factor bounding the batch/sequential posterior std ratio; sub-linear in batch size B, related to max information gain from B samples

conditions: f_c ~ GP(0,k_c) independently for each category
Assumption 1: GP sample-path partial derivatives satisfy P(|df/dx_i|<L) >= 1 - d r exp(-L^2/s^2)
Assumption 2: maximum information gain gamma_T ~ O(T^alpha) with 0 <= alpha < 1
T = number of rounds x batch size B (total function evaluations)

source.quote: Under Assumptions 1 and 2, the Bayesian regret for our method after $T$ iterations in the batch setting is given as $\text{BayesRegret}\left(T\right)\leq\mathcal{O}\left(\psi_{B}\sqrt{CT^{\alpha+1}\text{log}T}\right)$

results.notes: T counts total function evaluations. psi_B from Desautels et al. (2014).
